title: Embedding profiles graceful synchronization and SLI-driven rollouts
creator: Nina Park
description: Background: We need a robust, observable, and tenant-safe process to introduce new embedding models and model variants into the production reranking and embedding endpoints. Current ad-hoc onboarding has caused uneven latency regressions and surprises for high-throughput tenants. Goal: standardize model profiles, automated compatibility checks, and an SLI-driven staged rollout that protects latency and quality while enabling fast adoption of improved embed models.
problem_statement: New embedding variants cause three recurring issues: silent quality regressions (mismatched similarity scale), unexpected P95 latency tail increases under batching, and failures in reranking pipelines due to dimensionality or tokenization differences. We need an onboarding flow that detects these issues before wide rollout and enforces safe traffic ramps with automatic fallback.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a 'profile sync' workflow: publish model profiles (dimensionality, normalization, tokenization-hash, expected cosine distribution), run automated contract tests and offline rerank evals, then launch an SLI-driven staged rollout with gated ramping and automatic rollback triggers. Provide tenant opt-in pins and an emergency alias to route back to the previous production variant.
detailed_changes: Add model profile schema to catalog service: fields for embed_dim, norm_mode, tokenizer_hash, expected_similarity_quantiles, recommended_batch_size
Implement compatibility shim that verifies incoming embeddings shape + normalization at gateway and rejects incompatible requests with a clear error code for users
Create offline evaluation job that computes recall@k, MRR, MAP on curated golden sets and produces delta reports vs baseline
Extend routing layer to support percent-based tenant-scoped traffic pins and staged ramp policy with hold windows
Add SLI hooks: live recall@10 proxy (golden queries), latency_p50/p95, tail_batch_wait_ms, cache_hit_rate, and error_rate. These are used by rollout gates
Integrate automatic fallback: if SLIs exceed abort thresholds for two consecutive windows, rollback to previous alias and open a rollback incident ticket
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal vetting: run offline evals against 5 canonical datasets and synthetic tail workloads
Phase 1 - Canary: 0.5% traffic, 24 hour hold, validate SLIs and manual inspection of top-50 mismatched queries
Phase 2 - Early adopters: 5% traffic for tenants on opt-in list, 48 hour hold with automated golden-query checks
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp: 25% then 50% with 24 hour holds and SLI evaluation; abort on defined thresholds
Phase 4 - Full: 100% traffic and deprecation countdown for legacy alias
abort_conditions: live recall@10 drops by >3 percentage points vs baseline for two consecutive windows
latency_p95 increases by >30% and absolute p95 > 300ms for two consecutive windows
embedding_dim_mismatch_rate > 0.1% or gateway rejection rate spikes by >5x
error_rate for reranking endpoint > 0.5% sustained for 30 minutes
acceptance_criteria: Profile schema implemented and documented in model catalog
Compatibility shim returns deterministic error codes and is enabled in staging
Offline evaluation produces delta report and passes on >=80% of golden queries with no regressions beyond thresholds
Routing supports tenant-scoped percent pins and staged ramp automation is runnable from Console
Alerting and auto-rollback are wired to runbooks and on-call rotations
Performance benchmark: no more than 10% increase in median latency and p95 under 300ms for non-batched median workloads during canary
migration_steps: 1) Add new model variant to catalog with profile and alias 'model-x.v2'
2) Run nightly offline eval job and review delta report in PR
3) Deploy compatibility shim to staging + run integration tests for reranking pipeline
4) Open tenant opt-in list and invite five low-risk tenants for early adopter phase
5) Execute staged rollout via routing automation; monitor SLIs and perform manual QA checks
6) Complete deprecation notice email sequence and update docs for legacy alias
deprecation_schedule: Legacy alias 'model-x.v1' will enter deprecation after 30 days of full v2 traffic. Tenants will have a 180-day grace period to opt back or migrate. Automatic fallback remains available during grace period.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Quality regressions undetected by offline tests. Mitigation: require live golden-query proxy check before any >5% ramp
Risk: Latency tail due to batching differences. Mitigation: synthetic tail load tests and enforce recommended_batch_size in profile
Risk: Silent failures for tenants with custom vector post-processing. Mitigation: compatibility shim with explicit rejection and docs for post-processing guidance
related_prs_and_artifacts: GitHub PR #2149 - catalog: profile schema and validation
GitHub PR #2157 - routing: tenant pin support and ramp automation
qa_plan: Unit tests for profile parser and compatibility shim
Integration tests across gateway -> rerank worker -> store
Synthetic load tests for batched and single-request patterns
Shadow testing on 1% traffic before canary to validate no silent failures
notes: We need coordination with Customer Success to seed the early-adopter tenant list
Consider exposing a temporary per-tenant similarity-scaling factor if models show distributional shift
Future: hook this flow into Optimize recommendations to auto-suggest quantization/batching profiles
